content.user_title: Draft Prior Authorizations and Insurance Appeals
content.value_statement: US billing teams must organize payer requirements, clinical evidence, and denial responses. This guide helps AI assistants draft authorization packets, appeal letters, and tracking logs for professional review.
actual_capabilities: Guides drafting payer-specific prior authorization packets using supplied codes, clinical justification, and document requirements.
Helps classify denial reasons as administrative or medical necessity issues.
Organizes responses into corrected claims, reconsideration, formal appeals, or peer-to-peer review.
Guides drafting appeal letters with clinical arguments and supplied payer policy citations.
Supports preparing clinical arguments for peer-to-peer reviews.
Helps structure authorization and denial logs with case status and deadlines.
limitations: Covers US payers only; current payer policies require independent verification.
Provides a public guide only; original package scripts, extension source, and templates are absent.
Includes no implemented payer lookup, submission integration, or persistent tracking system.
Uses practice-provided codes and findings; drafts require billing specialist or clinician review and are not clinical or legal advice.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Prior Authorization Packet
use_cases.description: Organize supplied codes, clinical justification, and payer document requirements into a reviewable authorization draft.

use_cases.title: Draft a Medical Necessity Appeal
use_cases.description: Turn a denial notice, documented clinical findings, and verified payer policy into a structured first-level appeal.

use_cases.title: Prepare for Peer-to-Peer Review
use_cases.description: Summarize documented treatment history and policy criteria into clinical talking points for a payer review.

prompt_templates.title: Classify a Denial
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify this de-identified denial as administrative or medical necessity: [denial text]. Suggest the response route and identify missing information without inventing facts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: identify the next review step.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Authorization Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a prior authorization packet using these supplied codes, clinical findings, and verified payer requirements: [details]. List missing documents separately.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an Evidence-Based Appeal
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a first-level appeal using this de-identified denial, clinical documentation, and verified policy excerpt: [materials]. Use only supplied facts and flag missing evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: connect documented evidence to payer criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Organize a Denial Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a tracking log from these de-identified cases: [cases]. Group denials by payer and supplied code, recommend response routes, and prepare peer-to-peer talking points.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate several cases for team review.

output_examples.input: Draft an appeal for de-identified Case A, CPT 64493, denied for medical necessity. Supplied notes document six weeks of unsuccessful physical therapy.
output: Denied service: CPT 64493. Stated denial basis: medical necessity.
The supplied notes document six weeks of unsuccessful physical therapy. We request reconsideration based on the enclosed clinical documentation.
Before submission: add verified payer policy criteria, required identifiers, relevant records, and reviewer approval.

output_examples.input: Organize Case B: Payer Example, denial for missing authorization, corrected claim under review. No deadline was provided.
output: Denial category: administrative | Reason: missing authorization
Next review: verify the payer's authorization correction or reconsideration requirements.
Deadline: not supplied; verify against the denial notice.

best_practices: Use de-identified cases unless your organization has approved the AI environment for protected health information.
Verify current payer requirements, policy citations, and deadlines before submitting any draft.
Have a billing specialist or clinician review every code, clinical assertion, attachment, and response route.
anti_patterns: Inventing codes, treatment dates, clinical findings, or payer policy citations to complete a packet.
Submitting generated drafts without checking documentation, payer requirements, and professional approval.
Treating a generated tracking log as an automatically synchronized payer or practice management system.

faq.question: Does the skill select CPT or ICD-10 codes?
faq.answer: No. The guide specifies using codes and clinical findings supplied by the practice.

faq.question: Does it retrieve current payer policies?
faq.answer: The supplied folder contains no implemented policy retrieval tool. Provide verified policy materials and confirm current requirements before submission.

faq.question: Can it submit authorizations or appeals?
faq.answer: No submission integration is included. It helps prepare drafts for review and submission through your existing workflow.

faq.question: Can I include patient information?
faq.answer: Use de-identified information unless your organization approves the AI environment for protected health information. The guide does not establish privacy compliance.

faq.question: Does it replace clinical or legal review?
faq.answer: No. Outputs are working drafts for billing specialists or clinicians, not clinical or legal advice.

faq.question: Are tracking scripts and original templates included?
faq.answer: No. This folder contains only SKILL.md. It describes structured logs but omits the original package scripts, extension source, and templates.
